name: MYO5A (lavender foal)
summary: MYO5A encodes myosin Va, a motor protein that carries pigment granules to the edge of pigment cells and vesicles within nerve cells. A single-base deletion in exon 30 (c.4249del, p.Arg1417Alafs*13; g.139290592del on chromosome 1, EquCab3.0) shifts the reading frame and leaves no working protein. Two copies cause lavender foal syndrome, also called coat colour dilution lethal: a foal born with a pale, diluted coat and severe neurological signs that dies or is put down shortly after birth. It is recessive, and carriers are healthy and look normal. It is chiefly a disease of Arabian horses, above all Egyptian lines, and turns up in some Arabian-derived populations. No MYO5A allele is known to give a healthy diluted horse, and no effect on build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: MYO5A (lavender foal) carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. The horse is healthy and looks normal, and passes the copy to half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: Lavender foal syndrome
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The foal is born with a diluted coat - lavender, pale pink, silver or pale grey, the shade varies - and with severe neurological signs: seizures, flickering eyes, stiff paddling legs, the neck and back arched rigidly backwards, and no ability to stand or nurse properly. It dies or is put down shortly after birth.

Arabian, not of Egyptian descent (1 carrier in 56 horses, 1.8%, in the mapping study, Brooks et al. 2010; allele frequency 0.89%)
